edges.description: A meta-exposure rather than an exposure: it asserts that environmental context matters across subtypes without naming a context. Recorded as modulating for that reason, and graded partial on a sentence that reports what a panel of experts discussed. It is drawn because the claim it makes, that environment modifies trajectories across all subtypes, is the umbrella-level statement this entry exists to hold. This entry is the retained umbrella for diabetes mellitus and carries a single pathophysiology node, the shared hyperglycemia that every subtype converges on, so one target is the only shape available; the subtype-specific routes are modeled in the per-type entries and in the diabetic_vascular_complications module. Stated once here rather than repeated on all nine links, which lets each description carry its own reasoning.
edges.source: Environmental determinants of diabetes susceptibility and progression

edges.description: The autoimmune route to this node, kept deliberately general because the entry is the umbrella: the specific triggers are curated in Type_I_Diabetes, where the viral evidence is far deeper than anything here. Graded partial because the cited sentence says these triggers are thought to induce the autoimmune process, which is a belief about a mechanism rather than a measured effect.
edges.source: Exogenous triggers of islet autoimmunity in type 1 diabetes pathways

edges.description: The clearest causal exposure in this entry, because the drug produces the disease rather than raising the chance of it, and because stopping the drug often reverses it. That reversibility is the strongest causal design available anywhere in this entry, and the second item carries it along with its own limit, that persistence depends on treatment duration, agent and body mass.

A specific instance of diabetogenic pharmacotherapy that earns its own edge because the mechanism differs: checkpoint blockade releases the brakes on self-reactive T cells and the result is insulin deficiency, sometimes presenting abruptly in ketoacidosis, rather than the insulin resistance most diabetogenic drugs produce. Graded partial because the only evidence is a single case report.

Graded identically to the general islet-autoimmunity exposure and to the early-dietary one, because all three rest on the same sentence of the same paper, which names dietary factors and viruses together. None can be placed above the others on evidence held here.

Recorded as modulating rather than predisposing, which separates it from the viral link despite their sharing a sentence. The exposure's own description and effect field both frame early feeding as modulating the risk of islet autoimmunity in susceptible populations rather than initiating it, and the randomized evidence on infant feeding curated in Type_I_Diabetes is negative.

Traverses the same adiposity to insulin-resistance route as the high-calorie link and so takes the same link type, even though its own sentence names no intermediate: the schema asks whether the field knows the intervening steps, not whether the quoted sentence recites them. The thinness of the evidence is carried by the partial grade on the item instead, which places sedentary lifestyle in the epidemiology of metabolic syndrome rather than following it to insulin resistance.

The insulin-resistance route to this node, and the one exposure whose own sentence recites the intervening step: excess caloric intake driving hyperinsulinemia and the metabolic dysfunction of insulin resistance. That is why the item reads well, not why the link type is known; the other two adiposity exposures share the same route and now share the same link type. Graded partial because the sentence offers the step as a clinically valuable concept rather than a measurement.

The broadest of the three adiposity exposures and originally the thinnest-evidenced, resting on a screening recommendation alone. The route is the same well-mapped one the other two take, so the link type follows what the field knows rather than what any one sentence states. That recommendation alone would have left the edge asserting a mechanism no cited sentence described, so a second item was added that does describe it, naming excess body fat as the acquired cause of insulin resistance and insulin resistance as a route to type 2 diabetes.

nodes.description: Sustained hyperglycemia is the shared, subtype-independent driver of diabetic tissue injury across every form of diabetes mellitus. Whatever the upstream route (autoimmune beta-cell destruction in type 1, insulin resistance with beta-cell secretory failure in type 2, undernutrition-associated beta-cell impairment in type 5, or a monogenic beta-cell defect), chronic hyperglycemia feeds one conserved cascade: hyperglycemia-induced oxidative and AGE-RAGE stress, endothelial dysfunction and vascular inflammation, micro- and macrovascular injury, and diabetic end-organ complications (kidney disease, retinopathy, neuropathy, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease). That cascade is captured once in the diabetic_vascular_complications module, to which this node conforms; the per-type entries elaborate their own routes to hyperglycemia.

evidence.snippet: According to the World Health Organization (WHO) diabetes mellitus is a chronic, metabolic disease characterized by elevated levels of blood glucose, which leads over time to damage to the heart, vasculature, eyes, kidneys and nerves.

nodes.description: Exposure to medications with diabetogenic effects can precipitate persistent or transient diabetes phenotypes.

evidence.snippet: The DIDM is considered to be reversible after discontinuation of diabetogenic treatment, but there is a risk of persistence, which is related to the duration of treatment, prescribed medication, and body mass index.
